facts.raw_span: A 67-year-old man
hypertension, dyslipidaemia, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, active smoking (35 pack-years), a family history of ischaemic heart disease
prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF
left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities
patent stents in the circumflex artery, non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
new QTc prolongation to 500 ms

concepts.why: The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and presents with angina and ST-segment elevation, indicating acute coronary syndrome.
The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and presents with ST-segment elevation, indicating myocardial infarction.
The patient presents with ST-segment elevation, QTc prolongation, and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, which are consistent with takotsubo syndrome.
The patient presents with recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, indicating ventricular tachycardia.
The patient has a history of hypertension, dyslipidaemia, and smoking, and presents with significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis, indicating coronary artery disease.
The patient presents with ventricular fibrillation and requires cardiopulmonary resuscitation, indicating cardiac arrest.
The patient has a history of hypertension.
The patient has a history of stage 3 chronic kidney disease.
The patient has a history of dyslipidaemia.
The patient has a history of active smoking.
It explains the uncovered finding of left ventricular ejection fraction of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities, which is a characteristic feature of this condition.
It explains the uncovered finding of subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch, which is a characteristic feature of this condition.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with ST-segment elevation, recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, and ventricular fibrillation, along with new QTc prolongation and severely reduced LVEF after an initial normal echocardiogram, is most consistent with Takotsubo Syndrome, especially given the akinesia of all apical segments and hyperkinesia of the basal segments.
